units.title: European Exploration and the African slave trade 1500–1800

cards.title: Motives for European Expansion
body: Economic Reasons- from the 14th C onwards, land routes to Asia were blocked by the Byzantine Empire forcing the Europeans to look for new sea routes to expand trade with the East, especially for spices.
Cultural and ideological motives- the pretext used by the Europeans to justify their actions of expansion was to introduce Christianity to the pagan natives outside Europe.
The Three G’s- the three Gs stand for: God (the introduction of Christianity), Glory (praise for their countries), and Gold (wealth).

cards.title: Portugal
body: Portugal dominated the expeditions for exploration because they had superior weapons and knowledge of sea travel.

Prince Henry (The Navigator)- sponsored Portuguese ships along the West African coasts in 1420 and discovered The Gold Coast (present day Ghana), he further provided sailors with support and training.
Bartholomew Diaz- reached the southern tip of South Africa known as The Cape of Good Hope in 1488,
Vasco Da Gama- sailed into India through the Cape in 1497-1498 and returned to Portugal with cargos of spices. The profit he made from the cargos encouraged Portuguese traders to sail into India.
The Portuguese destroyed Arab-Turkish ships and defeated the Turkish and Indian fleet in 1509. They set up trade ports in Goa (India) and the Malay Peninsula and monopolized the spice trade.
Despite their trading posts in Asia, they weren’t powerful enough to colonize large areas in Asia.

cards.title: Spain
body: Unlike the Portuguese who reached Asia through the Indian Ocean (eastward), the Spanish tried to reach Asia through the Atlantic Ocean (westward).

Christopher Columbus- was an Italian explorer who sought financial help from Queen Isabella of Spain to reach Asia by sailing westwards. Believing he had reached Asia; he discovered the Americas by mistake in 1492.
Amerigo Vespucci- from Florence, Italy, sailed into the Americas and recognized them new undiscovered lands by writing letters about his voyages. The Americas were named after him.

Europeans called the Americas, The New World, b/c they were opportunities for conquest and exploitation, even though these lands had been homes to ancient civilizations such as the Maya, Aztec, and Inca for centuries.

Ferdinand Magellan- was a Portuguese sea Captain who circumnavigated the world by passing through the southern tip of South America and the Pacific in 1519 under the Spanish flag. He was killed in the Philippine islands.
Border conflict arose between Spain and Portugal regarding their colonies in the Americas, which was resolved by The Line of Demarcation in the Treaty of Tordesillas, 1494.

The Line of Demarcation was an imaginary line that divided their spheres of influence. Unexplored territories east of the line were given to Portugal along with Brazil and the routes to Africa while Spain was given the right over the Americas (west) with the exception of Brazil.

cards.title: The Spanish Empire
body: Spanish Conquistadores (conquerors) brought the end of the American civilizations using guns. In Meso-America, Hernan Cortes was able to destroy the Aztec Empire within three years while Francisco Pizarro took control of the Incan Empire in South America and set up the Spanish colonial administration under the reign of Queen Isabella.

The Native Americans were exposed to European diseases such as Small pox, measles and typhus, which they had no resistance to. Many were massacred by the Conquistadores while those who remained were forced to work on the sugar plantations and the mines owned by the Spanish
In order to destroy the Native American culture, Catholic missionaries began to convert them into Christianity and introduced European social structures, languages and government system.

cards.title: European rivals
body: By the end of the 16th C, NEW European rivals began to compete for the Eastern trade.
In the East, the Spanish controlled the Philippine islands in addition to their territories in the Americas.
English fleet landed in the northwestern coasts of India and set up colonies along the eastern coasts of North America and the plantations of the Caribbean in the 17th C

The Dutch (Netherlands) formed the East Indian Company in 1595 and begun to compete with England and France. In the West, The Dutch trade Empire in the Americas declined due to the rivalries with the English and the French. Their colony New Netherland (modern New York) was seized by the English along with Virginia, Massachusetts Bay, the eastern coasts of North America and set up sugar plantations in the Caribbean.
During the 1600s, the French colonized parts of the modern-day Canada and the state of Louisiana (North America).

cards.title: Effects of European Expansion
body: Growth of European Economy- Europe imported agricultural products such as potatoes, maize, tobacco, chocolate and sugar cane, large quantities of gold and silver from the American mines. Gold and silver were used as currency.

Decline of European cities- major trade routes shifted from the Mediterranean region to the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in the decline of the Italian and German city states and the rise of Atlantic trade ports.
Population growth- Western Europe’s population grew with the availability of additional food supply causing Urbanization.
Establishment of American Colonies- 16th C, Europeans established many trade colonies in the Americas. The Colonies were new territories in North America under direct government control.

The development of international trade- the rise of the American trade colonies led to the rise of international trade and commercial Capitalism. The colonies became the sources of raw materials and markets for finished goods.
A Colony is a settlement of people living in the new territory linked to the parent country by trade and direct government control.

**Step 1:** From the lesson: “Bartholomew Diaz- reached the southern tip of South Africa known as The Cape of Good Hope in 1488,”

**Step 3:** So the answer is D) Bartholomew Diaz.

cards.title: Model answer: motives for European exploration
cards.problem: (Exam question) Explain the motives behind European exploration in the 15th–16th centuries.

steps.text: Economic: from the 14th century the land routes to Asia were blocked, so Europeans looked for sea routes, especially for spices.
Religious/ideological: they claimed to bring Christianity to non-Christian peoples.
The "three Gs" summarise the motives: God (Christianity), Glory (prestige for their countries) and Gold (wealth).
Portugal led because it had superior weapons and knowledge of sea travel, with support from Prince Henry the Navigator.

cards.answer: Mainly economic (sea routes to Asian spices), plus religion and national glory – "God, Glory and Gold".

lessons.title: Africa During the Era of the Slave Trade

cards.title: The Slave Trade
body: Slavery had been practiced all over the world since the ancient times. In Africa, slaves were the prisoners of war and were sold as domestic workers to Arabia. Europeans sought gold in Africa until they began trading slaves.
16th C, sugar plantations grew in Brazil and the Caribbean and they needed labor but the native laborers had low immunity. This increased the demand for African slaves.
In 1518, the Spanish first shipped African slaves to the Americas and over the next 2 centuries the trade grew into a triangular trade connecting Europe, Africa, and America.

The Triangular Trade- European merchants brought manufactured goods such as guns and clothes to Africa and traded them for cargos of slaves who were sold in the Americas. Then they took raw materials such as tobacco, molasses (used to refine raw sugar), sugar, and raw cotton from the American plantations to Europe for manufacturing.

About 12-15 million African slaves were brought into the Americas between the 16thC-19thC. One of the reasons for the high numbers was high death rate among the slaves due to diseases, hunger and harsh working environment.

During the early years, Europeans bought slaves from the African slave markets in the coasts in return for gold and guns. But as the demand for African slaves increased in the American plantations, they moved inland into African villages in search for slaves.

cards.title: Effects of Slave Trade
body: Depopulation in particular African regions.
Created an age gap in the African communities
Brought warfare (war) in Africa

cards.title: Political and social structures
body: Europeans didn’t have much direct influence in Africa except for the few places they settled in such as South Africa and Mozambique.

During the 16th C, monarchy was the most common government system in Africa. States like the kingdom of Benin were highly centralized, while the states of Ashanti were collections of small principalities but majority of the Africans lived in small political units like villages let by elders.
Foreign influences- European presence in Africa caused changes such as;
The shift of trade routes from the Sahara to the coasts weakened trans-Saharan trade empires such as the Songhai empire leading to the rise of a new Moroccan dynasty in the 16th C.
Religion was greatly influenced by foreigners; Islam had more impact than Christianity in Northern Africa and later spread west and east.
The Portuguese begun missionary activities in Africa to spread Christianity while the other Europeans were more interested in slave trade and economic exploitations.

**Step 3:** So the answer is D) New World..

**Step 2:** Portugal was the first European nation to explore the African coast in the 15th century and subsequently initiated the Atlantic slave trade, initially taking enslaved Africans to Europe and later to the Americas.

**Step 3:** So the answer is B) Portugal..

cards.title: Past exam (Model exam 2016)
cards.q: Which of the following was an effect of Slave trade in Africa?
cards.why:
**Step 1:** From the lesson: “The Portuguese begun missionary activities in Africa to spread Christianity while the other Europeans were more interested in slave trade and economic exploitations.”

**Step 2:** The Trans-Atlantic and Trans-Saharan slave trades led to a massive loss of human life and labor, causing significant population declines in many regions. It also caused political instability and disrupted local economies.

**Step 3:** So the answer is A) Decline population.

cards.title: Model answer: the triangular trade

steps.text: Leg 1: European merchants took manufactured goods such as guns and cloth to Africa.
Leg 2: they exchanged them for enslaved Africans, who were shipped to the Americas and sold to plantations.
Leg 3: raw materials – tobacco, molasses, sugar and raw cotton – were taken from the Americas to Europe for manufacturing.
Result: about 12–15 million Africans were taken to the Americas between the 16th and 19th centuries, causing depopulation in Africa.

cards.answer: Europe → Africa (goods), Africa → Americas (enslaved people), Americas → Europe (raw materials).
